subject: general
question: Which Article of the Constitution of India allowed citizens to reside and settle in any part of the territory of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 19**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 19(1)(e)** of the Constitution of India provides citizens the fundamental right to reside and settle in any part of the territory of India.
 
• This right is subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by the State in the interest of the general public or for the protection of Scheduled Tribes.
 
• It ensures freedom of movement and residence across the country to promote national unity and integration.
 
• The provision is part of the broader framework of Fundamental Rights enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Reasonable restrictions under Article 19(5) may include measures for protecting indigenous tribal populations and maintaining public order.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights:**

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are guaranteed under Part III of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They are enforceable by courts and are aimed at ensuring political and civil freedoms.
 
• Rights under Article 19 include freedom of speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
 
 
• **Reasonable Restrictions:**
 
 
• Rights under Article 19 are not absolute and can be restricted under Article 19(2) to 19(6).
 
• Restrictions are meant to safeguard public order, sovereignty, morality, and the interests of Scheduled Tribes.
 
 
 
• **Scheduled Tribes Protection:**
 
 
• Specific laws like the Fifth and Sixth Schedules of the Constitution protect tribal areas and their autonomy.
 
• These laws aim to preserve the cultural and economic interests of indigenous tribal populations.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• Amendments to Fundamental Rights require adherence to Article 368 of the Constitution.
 
• The judiciary plays a key role in interpreting these rights and ensuring they are not diluted arbitrarily.
